newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against both the dollar and the pound on Wednesday, reflecting international trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 19.9505 to the dollar from 19.9405 on Tuesday, and traded at a mean rate of 33.384 to the pound from 33.364 on Tuesday.
Forex dealers said the rupee's fixing was in line with the stronger dollar in overnight international markets.
"Things are quiet in the local interbank forex market and (commercial) banks are still in long positions," one dealer said.
The dealer added that activity in the interbank forex market was subdued as banks preferred to wait and buy hard currencies at lower rates during central bank intervention.
Over the past few months, the central bank was seen selling dollars in the market at rates lower than the prevailing interbank ones to support the local currency.
Regular central bank intervention coupled with lower importer demand during the end of year lull, resulted in commercial banks holding long positions, dealers said.
